## 1. Overview & Profile

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| Official Name | The Options Clearing Corporation |
| Abbreviation | OCC |
| Website | [https://www.theocc.com](https://www.theocc.com) |
| Year Established | 1973 |
| Country / City | United States / Chicago, Illinois |
| Ownership Structure | Jointly owned by stockholder exchanges: Cboe Global Markets, Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE Arca, NYSE American), and Nasdaq (which holds ~40% following ISE acquisition). Originally five equal shareholders; Nasdaq's stake increased from 20% to 40% with ISE acquisition. |
| Parent Company / Group | None (independent market utility) |
| Regulatory Authority | SEC (primary regulator as a registered clearing agency), CFTC (secondary, as a registered Derivatives Clearing Organization), Federal Reserve Board (oversight under Dodd-Frank Title VIII as SIFMU) |
| CPMI-IOSCO PFMI Compliance | Yes — publishes PFMI Disclosure Framework and CPMI-IOSCO Public Quantitative Disclosures (PQD) quarterly |
| QCCP Status | Yes — recognized as a Qualifying CCP under Basel III framework for bank capital purposes |
| SIFMU Designation | Designated as a Systemically Important Financial Market Utility (SIFMU) by FSOC in July 2012 under Dodd-Frank Title VIII |

*Sources: [OCC — What Is OCC?](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/what-is-occ); [Wikipedia — Options Clearing Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Options_Clearing_Corporation); [OCC SIFMU Designation Press Release (2012)](https://www.theocc.com/about/newsroom/releases/2012/07_19.jsp); [OCC PFMI Disclosures](https://www.theocc.com/risk-management/pfmi-disclosures)*

### Key Historical Milestones

- **1973:** OCC founded as a clearing house for listed equity options on five exchanges, coinciding with the launch of the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE).
- **1975:** OCC began clearing put options (previously only calls were listed).
- **1985:** OCC began clearing index options.
- **1993:** OCC launched its Stock Loan/Hedge Program for securities lending transactions.
- **2000:** ENCORE clearing platform launched, replacing legacy systems.
- **2000:** Monthly volume record of 75.3 million contracts set in October.
- **2006:** STANS (System for Theoretical Analysis and Numerical Simulations) margin methodology implemented, replacing TIMS (Theoretical Intermarket Margin System).
- **2011 (August):** Record monthly volume of 550 million contracts; S&P lowered OCC credit rating to AA+ from AAA.
- **2012 (July):** Designated as SIFMU by FSOC under Dodd-Frank Title VIII.
- **2015:** OCC submitted Capital Plan to SEC for enhanced capitalization; subsequently challenged by non-shareholder exchanges.
- **2019 (February):** SEC disapproved OCC's Capital Plan on procedural and substantive grounds, citing insufficient information and governance concerns.
- **2019 (September):** SEC and CFTC charged OCC with failing to establish and maintain adequate risk management policies.
- **2019–2021:** Clearing Fund underfunding incident — OCC's Clearing Fund was underfunded by $200 million to $588 million at various times between October 2019 and May 2021 due to errors in the Liquidation Cost Model.
- **2022 (October):** SEC issued no-objection notice for OCC's Renaissance Initiative cloud infrastructure proposal.
- **2023 (February):** OCC settled with SEC ($17 million penalty) and CFTC ($5 million penalty) over Clearing Fund underfunding and operational risk management failures.
- **2024 (May 28):** Transition to T+1 settlement cycle for underlying equity securities.
- **2024:** Record-breaking annual volume — 12.2 billion options contracts cleared (+10.6% YoY), 60.1 million futures contracts (+7.7% YoY).
- **2025 (April 4):** Daily volume record of 102.6 million contracts, the first time exceeding 100 million in a single day.
- **2025 (October 10):** New daily volume record of 110 million option contracts cleared.

*Sources: [Wikipedia — Options Clearing Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Options_Clearing_Corporation); [OCC 2024 Volume Release](https://www.theocc.com/newsroom/views/2025/01-03-occ-annual-2024-and-december-2024-volume); [SEC Charges OCC (2023)](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2023-31); [CFTC Penalty Order (2023)](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/8661-23); [SEC Capital Plan Disapproval (2019)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2019/02/20/2019-02731/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-disapproving-proposed-rule)*

## 2. Clearing Model

### 2.1 CCP Services

OCC serves as the sole CCP for standardized equity options listed on U.S. national securities exchanges. It also clears futures, securities lending transactions, and certain OTC products.

| Product Class | Description | Volume / Scale (2024) |
|---------------|-------------|----------------------|
| **Equity Options** | Puts and calls on individual equities, ETFs | Majority of 12.2 billion total |
| **Index Options** | Options on equity indexes (e.g., SPX, NDX, VIX) | Included in total; SPX alone ~2+ billion |
| **Futures** | Futures on CBOE Futures Exchange (VIX futures, etc.) | 60.1 million contracts |
| **Securities Lending** | Stock Loan/Hedge Program and Market Loan Program | ~$139 billion average daily loan balance (June 2023 peak); ~9,800 transactions/day |
| **Single-Stock Futures** | Futures on individual equities | Minimal volume (largely dormant) |

*Sources: [OCC 2024 Volume Release](https://www.theocc.com/newsroom/views/2025/01-03-occ-annual-2024-and-december-2024-volume); [OCC Stock Loan Programs](https://www.theocc.com/clearance-and-settlement/stock-loan-programs); [FOW — OCC Securities Lending 30th Anniversary](https://www.fow.com/insights/3700860-occs-30th-anniversary-of-its-securities-lending-programme)*

### 2.2 Short-Dated and 0DTE Options

Short-dated options (contracts with less than one week to expiration) represent a rapidly growing segment of OCC's cleared volume:

- Short-dated options represented approximately **40% of total volume** in 2024
- Zero-day-to-expiry (0DTE) options represented approximately **20% of total volume** in 2024
- In SPX options specifically, 0DTE accounted for **48% of volume** in Q1 2024 (up from 11% five years prior)
- This rapid growth creates significant intraday risk management challenges, as 0DTE positions are currently uncollateralized intraday under traditional end-of-day margining

*Sources: [OCC 2024 Volume Release](https://www.theocc.com/newsroom/views/2025/01-03-occ-annual-2024-and-december-2024-volume); [SEC Filing SR-OCC-2024-010](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/occ/2025/34-102202.pdf)*

### 2.3 Novation Process

OCC uses an **open offer** model for novation. When an options trade is executed on a participant exchange and reported to OCC, OCC interposes itself as the CCP:

- OCC becomes the **buyer to every seller and seller to every buyer**
- This novation occurs at the point of trade acceptance
- OCC guarantees the performance of every cleared contract
- Positions are maintained at the clearing member account level

### 2.4 Netting

OCC performs multilateral netting:

- **Position Netting:** Long and short positions in the same series are netted at the account level
- **Premium Netting:** Daily premiums receivable and payable are netted into a single payment per clearing member
- **Exercise/Assignment Netting:** Delivery obligations from exercise and assignment are netted with NSCC through the "Accord" agreement

### 2.5 Clearing Membership

| Category | Details |
|----------|---------|
| Number of Clearing Members | ~115 |
| Member Types | U.S. broker-dealers, futures commission merchants (FCMs), U.S. banks (newly eligible), non-U.S. securities firms |
| Minimum Net Capital | $10,000,000 |
| Operational Requirements | Qualified staff, adequate facilities, ability to interface with OCC systems |
| Clearing Fund Contribution | Required; allocated based on risk-based methodology proportional to stress exposure |

In May 2023, the SEC approved OCC's amendment to expand eligible membership to include certain U.S. banks, in addition to the traditional broker-dealer and FCM categories.

*Sources: [OCC — Becoming a Clearing Member](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/becoming-a-clearing-member); [SEC Approval of Membership Standards Amendment (2023)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/05/11/2023-10029/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-granting-approval-of-proposed)*

### 2.6 Securities Lending Programs

OCC operates two distinct securities lending programs, established in 1993:

| Program | Model | Description |
|---------|-------|-------------|
| **Hedge Program** | Bilateral | Supports transactions executed bilaterally between counterparties; OCC acts as CCP guarantor |
| **Market Loan Program** | Exchange-based | Supports transactions originating through participating loan markets (e.g., AQS) |

- Since 2012, stock loan clearing volumes have grown at a **CAGR of 16%**, with open interest growing at **22%**
- OCC is the world's largest U.S. equities lending CCP
- OCC selected Axoni (DLT platform) to modernize securities lending infrastructure

*Sources: [OCC Stock Loan Programs](https://www.theocc.com/clearance-and-settlement/stock-loan-programs); [Axoni — OCC Modernization](https://axoni.com/press/occ-selects-axoni-to-modernize-securities-lending-infrastructure/)*

## 3. Risk Management

### 3.1 STANS Margin Methodology

OCC's **System for Theoretical Analysis and Numerical Simulations (STANS)** is the primary margin methodology, implemented in August 2006 to replace TIMS (Theoretical Intermarket Margin System). OCC was the **first derivatives clearinghouse in the world** to use a large-scale Monte Carlo-based risk management methodology.

#### STANS Technical Details

| Parameter | Details |
|-----------|---------|
| Methodology | Monte Carlo simulation — full portfolio margining |
| Risk Measure | 99% Expected Shortfall (ES) — average of all losses beyond the 99% VaR point |
| Enhanced Measure | 99.5% ES for the two single-factor sub-portfolios with greatest exposure; 99% ES for residual portfolio |
| Holding Period | **2-day liquidation horizon** (one day longer than U.S. competitors like CME) |
| Simulation Paths | Large-scale Monte Carlo simulations across all risk factors |
| Risk Factors | Equity prices, implied volatilities (by strike/maturity), interest rates, dividend yields, correlation structures |
| Pricing Models | Sophisticated options pricing models for all listed derivatives |
| Margin Components | Base component (ES) + Stress test add-on component |
| Stress Add-On | Considers ES increases from especially large market moves, perfect/zero correlations replacing estimated correlations, and extreme adverse idiosyncratic movements |
| Calculation Frequency | Daily (end-of-day), with intraday monitoring |

#### STANS vs. SPAN Comparison

| Feature | OCC STANS | CME SPAN |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| Methodology | Monte Carlo simulation | Scenario-based (16 risk scenarios) |
| Risk Measure | Expected Shortfall (99%) | Worst-case loss across scenarios |
| Portfolio Approach | Full portfolio margining with correlations | Product-group scanning with inter-commodity spreads |
| Holding Period | 2 days | 1 day (typically) |
| Non-linearity | Fully captured through simulation | Approximated via scanning range |
| Correlation Treatment | Dynamically estimated from historical data | Fixed inter-commodity spread credits |
| Computational Intensity | High (Monte Carlo) | Lower (parametric scenarios) |
| Historical Context | Introduced 2006 | Introduced 1988 |

*Sources: [OCC — Margin Methodology](https://www.theocc.com/Risk-Management/Margin-Methodology); [Risk.net — Clearing House of the Year: OCC](https://www.risk.net/awards/7930416/clearing-house-of-the-year-occ); [SEC STANS Approval Order (2006)](https://www.sec.gov/files/rules/sro/occ/34-53322.pdf)*

### 3.2 Margin Call Schedule

- **End-of-Day Margin:** Calculated daily after market close using STANS; margin calls issued overnight for next-morning settlement
- **Intraday Monitoring:** OCC monitors positions and market movements intraday and may issue intraday margin calls
- **Intraday Risk Charge (proposed/approved 2025):** New margin add-on to address uncollateralized intraday exposure, particularly from 0DTE options and overnight trading activity

*Sources: [SEC Approval of Intraday Risk Charge (April 2025)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/04/09/2025-06041/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-granting-approval-of-proposed)*

### 3.3 Default Waterfall

OCC's default waterfall describes the order in which financial resources are used to address losses arising from a clearing member default:

| Layer | Resource | Approximate Size |
|-------|----------|-----------------|
| 1 | **Defaulting member's margin deposits** | Varies by member (total margin pool ~$180–232 billion) |
| 2 | **Defaulting member's Clearing Fund contribution** | Proportional share of ~$19.5 billion total |
| 3 | **OCC's Skin-in-the-Game (SITG)** — OCC's own capital contribution | Persistent minimum of $69 million (capital) / ~$76 million (including deferred compensation); at least 25% of target regulatory capital |
| 4 | **Non-defaulting members' Clearing Fund contributions** (mutualized loss sharing) | Remainder of ~$19.5 billion Clearing Fund |
| 5 | **Assessments on non-defaulting members** (powers of assessment) | Up to the amount of each member's required Clearing Fund contribution (effectively doubling the mutualized pool) |
| 6 | **Recovery tools** (VMGH, partial tear-up, etc.) | See Section 3.5 |

**Cover 2 Standard:** OCC sizes its financial resources (margin + Clearing Fund) to cover the default of its **two largest clearing members and their affiliates** under extreme but plausible market conditions. This is consistent with CPMI-IOSCO PFMI Principle 4 for systemically important CCPs.

*Sources: [OCC — Default Rules & Procedures](https://www.theocc.com/risk-management/default-rules-and-procedures); [SEC Filing on Default Waterfall Amendments (2024)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/07/09/2024-14971/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-approving-proposed-rule-change); [Risk.net — OCC Cover 2](https://www.risk.net/risk-management/5843281/occs-move-to-cover-2-wont-cost-members-more-cro-says)*

### 3.4 Stress Testing & Back-Testing

**Stress Testing:**
- OCC performs **daily stress testing** of its financial resources
- Two categories of scenarios:
  - **Sizing Scenarios:** Assess whether collected resources are adequate and inform the size of OCC's financial resources
  - **Sufficiency Scenarios:** Measure potential exposures to determine whether additional margin or Clearing Fund calls are needed
- Scenarios include historical (e.g., 2008 financial crisis rally/decline variations), hypothetical, and reverse stress tests
- In 2024, OCC recategorized certain 2008-based Informational Scenarios as Sufficiency Scenarios after finding they consistently generated higher exposures
- In January 2025, SEC approved enhancements to STANS and Comprehensive Stress Testing (CST) methodology to better capture risks from short-dated options

**Back-Testing:**
- OCC conducts daily back-testing of its margin model
- In September 2024, SEC approved OCC's updated backtesting framework and establishment of a Resource Backtesting Margin Charge
- Back-testing compares actual portfolio P&L against margin requirements to validate model coverage

*Sources: [SEC Approval of Stress Testing Amendments (July 2024)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/07/09/2024-14971/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-approving-proposed-rule-change); [SEC Approval of STANS/CST Enhancements (January 2025)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/22/2025-01414/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-granting-approval-of-proposed); [SEC Approval of Backtesting Framework (September 2024)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/09/17/2024-21035/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-granting-approval-of-proposed)*

### 3.5 Recovery & Resolution Tools

OCC maintains a **Recovery and Orderly Wind-Down (RWD) Plan** that describes tools for managing losses and liquidity shortfalls beyond routine risk management:

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Assessments** | OCC may assess non-defaulting clearing members up to their required Clearing Fund contribution amount |
| **Variation Margin Gains Haircutting (VMGH)** | OCC can allocate losses to clearing participants that experience mark-to-market gains on their positions; provides incentive for members to participate in default management |
| **Voluntary Partial Tear-Up** | Members may voluntarily extinguish contracts to help OCC return to a matched book |
| **Mandatory Partial Tear-Up** | OCC authority to extinguish remaining contracts of a defaulted clearing member at OCC's marking price; used after other default management tools have been exhausted |
| **Orderly Wind-Down** | Planned cessation of critical services with transfer of positions to alternative clearing arrangements |

The RWD Plan was most recently amended and approved by the SEC in August 2025.

*Sources: [OCC Recovery and Orderly Wind-Down Plan](https://www.theocc.com/getmedia/e2cb031f-f53e-4c0b-981b-c3817bff79c9/GenUse_PartGuide_06182021.pdf); [SEC Approval of RWD Plan Modifications (August 2025)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/08/04/2025-14669/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-approving-proposed-rule-change); [FSB OCC Questionnaire](https://www.fsb.org/uploads/OCC-1.pdf)*

## 4. Settlement

### 4.1 Settlement Cycle

| Settlement Type | Cycle | Details |
|-----------------|-------|---------|
| **Premium Settlement** | T+1 | Payment of options premium is settled the next business day after trade date |
| **Exercise/Assignment (Equity Options)** | T+1 | Following the transition on May 28, 2024; previously T+2 |
| **Exercise/Assignment (Index Options)** | Cash settlement on T+1 | Cash-settled index options pay/receive cash difference |
| **Futures** | Daily mark-to-market | Variation margin settled daily; final settlement at expiration |
| **Stock Loan** | Same-day or T+1 | Depending on program and initiation time |

### 4.2 DVP and Settlement Finality

- **Exercise/Assignment of Equity Options:** When equity options are exercised/assigned, the resulting stock delivery obligation is processed through the **Accord** — an agreement between OCC and NSCC (National Securities Clearing Corporation)
- Under the Accord, NSCC accepts "E&A/Delivery Transactions" resulting from OCC exercise and assignment for clearing and settlement through NSCC's Continuous Net Settlement (CNS) system
- Settlement of underlying shares occurs at the **Depository Trust Company (DTC)** on a DVP (Delivery versus Payment) basis
- Settlement is considered **final and irrevocable** once completed through DTC's book-entry system

### 4.3 Premium Settlement Process

1. At end of each trading day, OCC calculates net premium obligations for each clearing member
2. Net premiums receivable and payable are aggregated across all cleared trades
3. Settlement occurs on T+1 through Fedwire or commercial bank payment systems
4. OCC may call for intraday premium settlement during periods of high volatility

### 4.4 Exercise and Assignment Process

1. **Exercise Notice:** Option holder's clearing member submits exercise notice to OCC (either by instruction or automatic exercise for in-the-money options)
2. **Assignment:** OCC uses a **random assignment algorithm** to distribute exercise notices fairly among clearing members with short positions in the assigned series
3. **Delivery/Cash Settlement:** For equity options, the resulting buy/sell obligations flow to NSCC via the Accord for settlement at DTC. For index options, cash settlement amounts are calculated and settled directly through OCC
4. **Automatic Exercise:** Options expiring in-the-money by $0.01 or more are automatically exercised unless contrary instructions are received

*Sources: [OCC Equity Options Product Specifications](https://www.theocc.com/clearance-and-settlement/clearing/equity-options-product-specifications); [OCC T+1 Info Memo #54580](https://infomemo.theocc.com/infomemos?number=54580); [SEC — OCC/NSCC Accord Modifications (2024)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/03/19/2024-05734/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-notice-of-no-objection-to-advance)*

## 5. Technology & Infrastructure

### 5.1 Core Systems

| System | Function | Status |
|--------|----------|--------|
| **ENCORE** | Core clearing, risk management, and data management platform; real-time processing engine | Legacy — operational since 2000; scheduled for replacement by Ovation |
| **Ovation** | Next-generation cloud-based clearing, settlement, risk management, and data platform | In testing; external beta testing began July 2024; launch targeted for mid-2025 [unverified if completed] |
| **STANS** | Margin calculation engine (Monte Carlo-based) | Active — continuously enhanced |
| **CLEARS** | Clearing member reporting and inquiry system | Active [unverified current status] |

### 5.2 ENCORE Architecture

- **Monolithic architecture** — tightly coupled components making change difficult
- Runs in traditional on-premises data centers
- Receives trade and post-trade data from exchanges on a transaction-by-transaction basis in real time
- Maintains clearing member positions, calculates margin and Clearing Fund requirements
- Provides reporting to OCC staff, regulators, and clearing members

### 5.3 Ovation Architecture (Renaissance Initiative)

OCC's **Renaissance Initiative** is a multi-year technology modernization program to replace ENCORE with the Ovation platform:

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| Cloud Provider | Amazon Web Services (AWS) |
| Architecture | Modular, cloud-native; three pillars — Clearing & Settlement, Data, Risk Management |
| Real-Time Processing | Stream processing using Apache Kafka and Apache Flink |
| Data Processing | Prices for over 2 million financial instruments per second; billions of open option positions |
| Disaster Recovery | Isolated Kafka + Flink infrastructure in both AWS and on-premises data center |
| Key Benefits | Enhanced resiliency, security, scalability; real-time risk measurement using current prices (vs. prior-day close) |

**Renaissance Timeline:**
- **October 2022:** SEC no-objection notice for cloud infrastructure proposal
- **2023:** Ovation development and internal testing
- **July 2024:** External beta testing commenced (Beta 1)
- **October 2024:** Beta 2 launched with expanded functionality
- **January 2025:** Beta 3 — collateral management testing
- **Mid-2025:** Planned Ovation launch (ENCORE-to-Ovation conversion in single processing cycle)

### 5.4 Processing Capacity

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Daily Peak Volume (record) | 110 million contracts (October 10, 2025) |
| Data Ingestion | >2 million instrument prices per second |
| Open Positions Tracked | Billions of open option positions |
| Participant Exchanges Supported | ~21 exchanges and trading platforms |

### 5.5 Interface Protocols

- **FIX/FIXML:** Industry-standard messaging for trade submission and reporting
- **Proprietary APIs:** OCC-specific interfaces for clearing member connectivity
- **Market Data Feeds:** Real-time position and margin data delivery

*Sources: [OCC Transformation](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/occ-transformation); [OCC — Clearing, Risk and Data Changes](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/occ-transformation/clearing-risk-and-data-changes); [Confluent Current 2024 — OCC Stream Processing](https://current.confluent.io/2024-sessions/how-the-worlds-largest-options-clearinghouse-moved-from-batch-to-stream-processing-to-manage-risk); [Built In Chicago — OCC Tech Infrastructure](https://www.builtinchicago.org/articles/chicago-options-clearing-corporation-tech-infrastructure); [Traders Magazine — OCC Ovation Testing](https://www.tradersmagazine.com/featured_articles/occ-gets-ready-for-ovations-testing/); [IBM — OCC Case Study](https://www.ibm.com/case-studies/options-clearing-corporation)*

## 6. Regulatory Framework

### 6.1 Regulatory Structure

| Regulator | Jurisdiction | Scope |
|-----------|-------------|-------|
| **SEC** | Primary regulator | Registered clearing agency under Section 17A of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934; clears put/call options on equity issues, stock indexes, foreign currencies, interest rate composites, and single-stock futures |
| **CFTC** | Secondary regulator | Registered Derivatives Clearing Organization (DCO); clears futures and options on futures |
| **Federal Reserve Board** | SIFMU oversight | Prudential oversight under Dodd-Frank Title VIII; access to Federal Reserve discount window and payment system services |
| **FSOC** | Designation authority | Designated OCC as SIFMU in July 2012 |

### 6.2 Key Regulatory Requirements

- **SEC Rule 17Ad-22(e):** Enhanced standards for covered clearing agencies (effective April 2017); establishes requirements for risk management, financial resources, governance, operations, and recovery planning
- **CFTC Core Principles:** Requirements for DCOs under the Commodity Exchange Act
- **PFMI Compliance:** OCC publishes PFMI Disclosure Framework and quarterly PQD data in accordance with CPMI-IOSCO guidance
- **Annual Financial Audit:** OCC's financial statements are audited annually
- **Regulatory Reporting:** Regular reporting to SEC, CFTC, and Federal Reserve on risk metrics, financial resources, and operational performance

### 6.3 Notable Regulatory Actions

| Year | Action | Details |
|------|--------|---------|
| **2019** | SEC & CFTC charges | Failure to establish and maintain adequate risk management policies; SEC fined OCC in connection with risk management deficiencies |
| **2019** | SEC Capital Plan disapproval | SEC disapproved OCC's proposed Capital Plan; cited insufficient information, governance concerns, competitive impact on non-shareholder exchanges |
| **2023 (Feb)** | SEC settlement | $17 million penalty for Clearing Fund underfunding (Oct 2019–May 2021); Clearing Fund was underfunded by $200M–$588M at various times |
| **2023 (Feb)** | CFTC settlement | $5 million penalty for operational risk management violations related to automated systems |

*Sources: [SEC Press Release — OCC Charges (2023)](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2023-31); [SEC/CFTC Press Release (2019)](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2019-171); [CFTC Press Release (2023)](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/8661-23); [SEC Capital Plan Disapproval (2019)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2019/02/20/2019-02731/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-disapproving-proposed-rule)*

## 7. Interoperability

### 7.1 Cross-Margining Programs

OCC maintains cross-margining agreements that allow hedged positions cleared at separate clearinghouses to be combined into a single portfolio for margin purposes:

| Program | Counterpart CCP | Description |
|---------|----------------|-------------|
| **OCC-CME Cross-Margin Program** | CME Clearing | Allows qualifying clearing members to offset equity option positions (OCC) against related equity index futures positions (CME); established after 1987 Black Monday crash; second amended and restated agreement approved in 2020 |

Cross-margining uses OCC's STANS methodology to calculate the combined portfolio risk, typically resulting in lower margin requirements than if margins were calculated separately at each CCP.

### 7.2 Cross-Guaranty and Linkages

| Arrangement | Details |
|-------------|---------|
| **OCC-NSCC Accord** | Governs the processing of physically settled equity options; NSCC accepts exercise/assignment delivery transactions for settlement through its CNS system at DTC |
| **Exchange Linkages** | OCC maintains Participant Exchange Agreements with all 16+ options exchanges; the Amended and Restated Participant Exchange Agreement was approved by the SEC in July 2025 |

### 7.3 Ongoing Coordination

OCC is evaluating adjustments to existing cross-CCP agreements and exploring potential new arrangements to support aligned margin cycles and risk management, particularly in light of:
- Extended trading hours initiatives
- T+1 settlement transition
- Growing intraday risk from 0DTE options

*Sources: [OCC — Cross Margin Programs](https://www.theocc.com/Risk-Management/Cross-Margin-Programs); [Yale SOM — Cross-Margining and Financial Stability](https://som.yale.edu/blog/cross-margining-and-financial-stability); [SEC Approval of Participant Exchange Agreement (July 2025)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/07/16/2025-13263/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-granting-approval-of-proposed)*

## 8. Fees

### 8.1 Clearing Fee Schedule

OCC's fee schedule has undergone several changes in 2024–2025:

| Fee Type | Amount | Effective Date |
|----------|--------|---------------|
| **Per Contract Clearing Fee (Options)** | $0.025 | Effective February 14, 2025 (increased from $0.02) |
| **Per Contract Clearing Fee (Futures)** | $0.025 [unverified — may differ] | -- |
| **Per Transaction Clearing Fee** | Removed | Previously $55.00 for transactions of 2,751+ contracts; eliminated February 2025 |
| **Minimum Monthly Clearing Fee** | $200.00 | Current |
| **Operational Loss Fee** | Variable; updated per Capital Management Policy | Per SEC filing SR-OCC-2024 |
| **Clearing Fee Holiday** | $0.00 (temporary) | December 1–31, 2025 |

**Fee History:**
- The average clearing fee per contract from June 2021 through November 2024 was approximately **$0.019 per contract** (including the effect of the now-removed Per Transaction Fee cap)
- The increase to $0.025 and removal of the per-transaction cap was designed to address OCC's anticipated cash flow needs based on interest rate forecasts, projected operating expenses, projected volumes, and capital needs
- OCC occasionally implements "fee holidays" when accumulated revenue exceeds targets — a one-month holiday was implemented in December 2025

### 8.2 Exercise and Assignment Fees

Specific exercise and assignment fees per contract are published in OCC's Schedule of Fees on [theocc.com](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/schedule-of-fees). [Exact amounts not publicly available in search results — refer to official schedule]

### 8.3 Membership Fees

- Initial and ongoing membership fees are assessed per OCC's By-Laws
- Clearing Fund contributions are required based on risk-based allocation methodology (not a flat fee)
- In 2016, OCC announced a $39 million refund to clearing members and ~$17 million dividend to stockholder exchanges, reflecting revenue surplus

*Sources: [OCC — Schedule of Fees](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/schedule-of-fees); [SEC Filing SR-OCC-2024-017 (Fee Change)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/12/27/2024-31089/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-notice-of-filing-and-immediate); [SEC Filing SR-OCC-2025-002 (Fee Update)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/02/24/2025-02944/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-notice-of-filing-and-immediate); [OCC Fee Holiday Info Memo #57379](https://infomemo.theocc.com/infomemos?number=57379)*

## 9. Recent Developments

### 9.1 Renaissance Initiative / Technology Modernization

OCC's multi-year **Renaissance Initiative** is the most significant technology transformation in its history:

- **Ovation platform** built on AWS cloud with modular architecture (clearing & settlement, data, risk management pillars)
- Transition from batch processing (ENCORE) to real-time **stream processing** using Apache Kafka and Flink
- Enables intraday risk calculation using current market prices rather than prior-day closing prices
- External industry testing began July 2024 with progressive beta releases
- Planned conversion from ENCORE to Ovation in a single processing cycle [target: mid-2025; completion status unverified as of April 2026]
- SEC no-objection on cloud infrastructure received October 2022

### 9.2 Extended Trading Hours

- Cboe and other exchanges have expanded or proposed extended trading sessions (pre-market and post-market) for equity options
- Cboe extended trading includes 7:30–9:25 a.m. ET and 4:00–4:15 p.m. ET sessions for select options classes
- OCC infrastructure must support clearing and risk management across extended hours
- Creates challenges for margin calculation timing, intraday risk exposure, and settlement cycle alignment

### 9.3 0DTE Options Growth Impact

The explosive growth of zero-day-to-expiry options has driven significant risk management adaptations:

- **Intraday Risk Charge:** SEC approved (April 2025) a new margin add-on applied to all clearing member accounts to mitigate risks from intraday and overnight trading activity
- **STANS Enhancements:** SEC approved (January 2025) changes to STANS and CST methodology to better capture short-dated options risks; average daily margin impact estimated at +0.58%
- **Volatility Adjustments:** OCC proposed (October 2024) a mechanism to adjust margin parameters during periods of high volatility
- OCC's intraday exposure to 0DTE options was previously **uncollateralized** — the new Intraday Risk Charge addresses this gap

### 9.4 Securities Lending Expansion

- OCC selected **Axoni** (distributed ledger technology platform) to modernize its securities lending infrastructure
- Stock loan clearing volumes have grown at a 16% CAGR since 2012
- OCC is now the world's largest U.S. equities lending CCP
- Programs expanded to support broader market participation and operational efficiency

### 9.5 2021 Capital Plan / Governance Crisis and Resolution

This episode represents a significant chapter in OCC's history:

**Timeline:**
1. **2015:** OCC submitted Capital Plan to SEC proposing significant capitalization increase through dividends to stockholder exchanges, funded by clearing fee increases
2. **2017:** SEC initially approved the Capital Plan
3. **2017:** D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals remanded the decision back to the SEC following challenge by non-shareholder exchanges (e.g., MIAX) who argued they were denied fair notice and opportunity to present views
4. **2019 (February):** SEC **disapproved** the Capital Plan, finding:
   - Insufficient evidence that the Plan was consistent with the Securities Exchange Act
   - Governance concerns — conflicts of interest between OCC management/board and stockholder exchanges
   - Failure to notify non-shareholder exchanges of the Plan's competitive significance
   - Questions about whether fee-funded dividends to owner-exchanges were appropriate for a market utility
5. **2019 (September):** SEC and CFTC separately charged OCC with risk management policy failures unrelated to the Capital Plan but occurring during the same period
6. **2019–2021:** Errors in OCC's Liquidation Cost Model led to Clearing Fund underfunding of **$200M–$588M** at various times
7. **2023 (February):** OCC settled with SEC ($17M) and CFTC ($5M); total penalties of $22M
8. **Post-2023:** OCC implemented remedial measures including enhanced governance, improved internal controls, new Capital Management Policy with regulatory capital target of $303 million, and persistent minimum SITG of $69 million

**Lessons:**
- Highlighted tensions in OCC's ownership model — stockholder exchanges as both owners and competitors of non-shareholder exchanges
- Led to enhanced regulatory scrutiny of OCC governance
- Prompted OCC to adopt more transparent capital management and fee-setting processes
- Reinforced the importance of robust internal controls at SIFMUs

### 9.6 Clearing Fund Methodology Reform (2025)

- In October 2025, OCC filed a proposed rule change to reform its Clearing Fund **allocation methodology** to better align contributions with the stress risk each clearing member poses to OCC
- In December 2025, SEC granted accelerated approval of the reformed methodology
- The new methodology ensures that stress-based risk is "fairly allotted to market participants that expose OCC to such stress risk"

### 9.7 Volume Records and Market Growth

- **2024:** 12.2 billion options contracts cleared (record; +10.6% YoY)
- **2025 (January):** 1.16 billion monthly contracts (+17.8% YoY)
- **2025 (April 4):** First-ever 100M+ daily volume — 102.6 million contracts
- **2025 (October 10):** New daily record of 110 million contracts
- Driven by retail participation, zero-commission trading platforms, 0DTE growth, and economic uncertainty

*Sources: [OCC Transformation](https://www.theocc.com/company-information/occ-transformation); [SEC Approval of Intraday Risk Charge (April 2025)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/04/09/2025-06041/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-granting-approval-of-proposed); [SEC Approval of STANS/CST Enhancements (January 2025)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/22/2025-01414/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-granting-approval-of-proposed); [SEC Capital Plan Disapproval (2019)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2019/02/20/2019-02731/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-order-disapproving-proposed-rule); [SEC Charges OCC (2023)](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2023-31); [Compliance Week — OCC Penalties](https://www.complianceweek.com/regulatory-enforcement/sec-cftc-order-options-clearing-corp-to-pay-22m-over-internal-rule-failures/32696.article); [FIA — OCC Capital Plan](https://www.fia.org/fia/articles/fia-questions-new-occ-capital-management-plan-sec-letter); [OCC 2024 Volume Release](https://www.theocc.com/newsroom/views/2025/01-03-occ-annual-2024-and-december-2024-volume); [SEC Clearing Fund Allocation Approval (December 2025)](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/12/16/2025-22855/self-regulatory-organizations-the-options-clearing-corporation-notice-of-filing-of-partial-amendment); [Cboe Extended Trading Hours FAQ](https://cdn.cboe.com/resources/membership/Equity_Options_Extended_Trading_Hours_FAQ.pdf)*

## Comparison with KRX Clearing

| Feature | OCC (U.S.) | KRX (Korea) |
|---------|------------|-------------|
| Role | CCP for listed options and futures | CCP for all KRX-listed products (equities, derivatives, bonds) |
| CSD | DTC (separate entity via NSCC Accord) | KSD (Korea Securities Depository — separate entity) |
| Margin Methodology | STANS (Monte Carlo, 99% ES, 2-day horizon) | KOSPI 200 options: SPAN-like; equities: VaR-based |
| Default Standard | Cover 2 (two largest members + affiliates) | Cover 1 [unverified] |
| SIFMU Equivalent | Yes (Dodd-Frank Title VIII) | Designated as systemically important by FSC/FSS |
| Settlement Cycle | T+1 (options premium, exercise/assignment) | T+2 for equities; T+1 for derivatives |
| Ownership | Exchange-owned (Cboe, NYSE, Nasdaq) | Part of Korea Exchange (government-designated) |
